can_answer: yes: the file can compare the yearly composition of reported motorist and cyclist deaths, although this normalized measure does not show annual fatality volume or risk.
metric: For each year, the percentage of combined reported motorist-plus-cyclist deaths attributed to each group; calculate each group's summed deaths divided by the sum of both groups' deaths, times 100.
denominator: Within each year, all reported motorist deaths plus all reported cyclist deaths (using the same complete crash rows for both sums).
population: All police-reported NYC motor vehicle crash records dated from 2013 through 2025; outcome counts are deaths of motorists or cyclists associated with those crashes.
filters: Crash date is in calendar years 2013–2025 inclusive.
Omit crash rows where either number_of_motorist_killed or number_of_cyclist_killed is NULL so both group totals use a common base; disclose the omission.
years: 2013–2025 inclusive, by calendar year of crash_date.
grouping: Calendar year and road-user group (motorist, cyclist).

data_check.facts: There are 2,132,218 in-range crash records across 2013–2025. In every requested year the file's first and last crash dates are January 1 and December 31, respectively. Neither death-count column has NULL values in any in-range row, so 0 records are omitted by the common-completeness filter. The fields are typed counts and crash_date is DATE typed; no in-range crash_date missing, string-unknown, or impossible values were found/representable; the source description specifies no default date sentinel.
data_check.decision: Keep records with both death-count values present and disclose the completeness check; this retains all 2,132,218 in-range crashes. Use the full 2013–2025 period because each year's date span includes both calendar boundaries. No plan change was needed.

limitations: This composition is only among reported motorist and cyclist deaths, normalizes away annual volume, and is not population-, travel-, or exposure-adjusted risk. Crash records with dates that are NULL cannot be assigned to the requested years; the in-range file date span reaches both calendar boundaries in every requested year.
